text: Around 2400 BCE lies within Caral’s broadly dated development. Platforms and circular gathering spaces orient us to the Supe Valley’s built landscape. They do not establish the same layout or activity in every year; the linked coastal food study has separately dated burial contexts.

Around 2400 BCE falls within the selected Saqqara wall’s museum date range and after Kerma’s approximate foundation. The chapel is evidence of elite funerary representation; Kerma offers a distinct Nubian urban history. The later beaker is a next reading, not an object from this same moment.

citations.locator: City of Kerma: c2500 BCE foundation

text: The 2400 BCE view uses Orkney’s broader 3000–2000 BCE monumental-landscape frame. It does not extend Skara Brae’s village occupation to this date. Read the earlier houses alongside burial and ceremonial monuments, whose individual construction histories remain separate.

citations.locator: Printed p17: modeled village ending 2545–2440 cal BCE

text: Around 2400 BCE sits within the museum’s Early Dynastic city-state frame. Uruk continued after the earlier spread of its material culture. The selected grain tablet is older: use it to investigate accounting practices, not as a direct record of this selected year.

Around 2400 BCE falls within the broad third-millennium Indus urban setting. Compare water management at Dholavira with wells and drainage at Mohenjo-daro. The view marks a regional comparison, not a claim that every visible structure at either site was operating in that exact year.

citations.locator: Brief synthesis: third-millennium settlement and urban systems

text: Around 2400 BCE lies within Liangzhu’s city-site frame and matches the approximate date assigned to the selected jade. Those overlapping dates make comparison possible; they do not establish that this museum object came from the city excavation or that every waterwork was built at this moment.

Around 2400 BCE is near Kuk’s rounded early Phase 3 boundary and within An Sơn’s estimated initial-occupation range. These are independent archaeological chronologies, not exact events in the selected year. An Sơn’s later houses and burials cannot all be assigned to its beginning. Lapita remains a later comparison.

Around 1200 BCE, Poverty Point and San Lorenzo provide distinct settlement settings. Caral’s retained development range has already ended. Compare the earthworks and evidence of provisioning without placing all three at one simultaneous peak.

The selected Nile setting around 1200 BCE is Egyptian administration in Nubia, including temple and settlement development. Kerma’s earlier kingdom and the beaker remain earlier readings. Political control did not make every local person, craft or experience identical.

citations.locator: Upper Nubia: c1500–1070 BCE; Key Events c1550–1070 BCE

text: Around 1200 BCE, the mainland Greek account describes destruction and declining palace institutions. British farming landscapes belong to a different, longer sequence. This comparison shows uneven change; it does not establish one event or cause across Europe.

Around 1200 BCE lies near the end of Hattusha’s broad capital-era frame. Its buildings represent multiple phases. Uluburun’s earlier cargo provides a separate exchange comparison, not a shipwreck dated to this selected year or proof of one cause of political change.

Around 1200 BCE falls within the cited 1400–1000 BCE Bhagwanpura phase. It is a later village setting, separate from Dholavira’s earlier urban occupation. The phase range does not date every house or pottery change to this exact year.

Around 1200 BCE lies within Yin Xu’s late-Shang capital frame. Palace, shrine, tomb and divination evidence offer related but distinct views of institutions. The later Shang–Zhou transition is not moved back to this snapshot date.

Around 1200 BCE belongs within the broad Bismarck Lapita frame and near the later boundary of An Sơn’s selected burial sequence. Remote Oceanian settlement and individual Tongan sites require their own later or overlapping dates. This snapshot does not establish one contemporaneous chain of settled islands.

citations.locator: Bismarck emergence and Remote Oceania 1100–800 BCE

text: Around 300 BCE, the museum chronology describes textile-wrapped burials on the Paracas Peninsula. This coastal setting supplies a dated comparison. Chavín’s conflicting summary endpoints remain unresolved; the selected museum textile is not assigned to a Paracas burial, and the later Colima case is not backdated.

citations.locator: Key Events c300 BCE: funerary bundles

text: Around 300 BCE marks the approach to the third-century BCE shift toward most royal burials at Meroe in UNESCO’s account. It is a broad transition marker, not an exact relocation event. Taharqo’s seventh-century BCE objects are earlier comparisons.

Around 300 BCE falls after Alexander’s death and within the emerging Hellenistic political setting. Earlier Athenian objects and institutional descriptions offer comparisons, not proof that every Greek city retained the same arrangements at this date.

Around 300 BCE belongs to the successor-kingdom setting after Alexander, including Seleucid power in the Near East. The Assyrian and Achaemenid palace readings are earlier institutional comparisons, not courts still ruling at this date.

Around 300 BCE belongs to the early Mauryan setting under Candragupta, shortly before the source’s approximate transfer to Bindusara. Ashoka’s later inscriptions are a next reading, not evidence already issued at this snapshot date.

citations.locator: Opening paragraphs: succession c297–298 BCE; Ashoka c268–232 BCE

text: Around 300 BCE lies within the Warring States period, before imperial Qin. Chu and Qin provide distinct political settings; the later standardization and Liye paperwork are comparisons across a transition, not documents from this selected year.

Around 300 BCE falls within the broad Đông Sơn-associated frame. Individual drums and deposits still need their own dates. In Tonga it is later than the study’s proposed end of pottery manufacture; that material boundary does not demonstrate that island communities ended.

citations.locator: Abstract and Discussion: manufacture ceased by c400 BCE

text: Around 200 CE, Teotihuacan, Ohio gathering traditions and Moche valley communities provide distinct regional settings. The broad overlap permits comparison, not the assignment of every later apartment, mound or workshop to this year.

Around 200 CE falls within the selected Aksumite and Meroe-region histories. The early Adulis account offers preceding evidence of coastal–inland exchange; Beta Samati’s later finds are follow-through, not objects automatically deposited in this year.

Around 200 CE belongs to Severan rule. Caracalla’s later citizenship grant in 212 CE has not yet occurred, and Constantinople’s later imperial history is not backdated. The portrait and household inquiry remain grounded in their own ranges.

Around 200 CE, Palmyra’s civic setting coexists with the late Parthian world. The Sasanian takeover of 224 CE comes later. These dates locate distinct institutions; they do not supply a journey taken by every object.

Around 200 CE lies within the broad Kushan frame. The selected coin and sanctuary inscriptions refer to separately dated earlier events and records; they are evidence for an institutional history, not proof that those works occurred in this year.

Around 200 CE belongs to Eastern Han, before the conventional 220 CE endpoint. Broadly dated tomb models support a household-provisioning inquiry. Chao Cuo’s much earlier proposal remains a comparison, not a regulation documented for this year.

Around 200 CE falls within the museum’s broad lower-Mekong Óc Eo frame. Its displayed fifth–seventh-century objects and later Luy Lâu workshop finds are not backdated. Tongan research separately describes settlement continuing into later aceramic periods; it does not identify an exact event in this year.

Around 850 CE marks the approximate beginning of Pueblo Bonito’s staged construction, not completion of the great house. The selected Maya cup is earlier; the sampled Chaco cacao vessels are later. Their comparison does not establish an exchange between those particular objects or communities in this year.

Around 850 CE lies within the excavation report’s 750–1100 high point for Djenné-Djeno and nearby settlements. This supplies a Middle Niger urban setting before the later Mali Empire. Aksumite deposits and the architecture of present Djenné retain their separate chronologies.

By 850 CE Aachen’s early ninth-century chapel had been built, while Constantinople stood shortly after the 843 restoration of icons. The present Aachen mosaic and the selected Byzantine ivory belong to later dates and do not illustrate this exact year.

In 850 CE the Abbasid court was in Samarra, within its 836–892 residence there. Baghdad’s founding in 762 and later changes in caliphal power are distinct events. A vessel’s broader catalogue range does not make it a documented product of this exact year.

Around 850 CE falls within Nalanda’s monastic history and after the foundation period attributed to Paharpur. The complete later layouts are not securely dated to this year, and Yijing’s seventh-century observations remain earlier testimony.

Around 850 CE lies within Tang and Silla histories, while Barhae also existed. Nara was no longer Japan’s capital, but its religious landscape continued; UNESCO dates the Kasugayama forest prohibition from 841. The selected earlier Tang tomb figure retains its own catalogue date.

Around 850 CE lies within Borobudur’s broad construction frame and the opening centuries of the Angkor regional frame. Later Angkor Wat is not backdated. The Tongan study separately documents continuity into aceramic periods, without identifying an event exactly in 850.

Around 1250 CE falls within Cahokia’s selected urban investigation frame but after Pueblo Bonito’s main construction range of about 850–1150. Chaco’s later changes are part of the comparison, not a claim that its entire great-house programme remained unchanged in 1250.

Around 1250 CE falls within Kilwa’s thirteenth–fourteenth-century prosperity and the occupation of Great Zimbabwe’s hill settlement. Husuni Kubwa and the Great Enclosure are later. The selected Middle Niger figure is broadly thirteenth-century, without a precisely documented 1250 find context.

Around 1250 CE follows the medieval development of Provins’s fairs and Fontenay’s twelfth-century church and ironworks. Constantinople was then under Latin rule, before the Byzantine recovery of 1261. Later restored fabric must remain separately labelled.

By 1250 CE Karakorum’s documented 1235 building programme lay in the past, while Baghdad remained before the Mongol conquest of 1258. Rubruck’s 1254 visit is a later observation, not an eyewitness report from this exact year.

Around 1250 CE is after the early Qutb building phases and the selected eleventh–twelfth-century Chola temple projects. Delhi’s Alai Darwaza of 1311 is still later. These local sequences do not establish one regional political or religious system.

Around 1250 CE belongs to Southern Song rule in the south alongside Mongol power farther north. It precedes the Yuan name of 1271, the final conquest of Southern Song in 1279 and the Ming beginning in 1368. Those later labels cannot be substituted for the selected year.

Around 1250 CE lies within Angkor’s regional history. For Aotearoa, 1250 is the beginning of a published North Island model interval of 1250–1275, not a verified arrival in this year. The South Island interval of 1280–1295 is later and remains separate.

citations.locator: Abstract and Timing of Polynesian Arrival

text: Around 1600 CE comes shortly after the San Agustín wreck of 1595, within an expanding Pacific colonial exchange system. Andean textile work also continued under colonial conditions. The selected 1450–1550 tunic and the later shipbuilding reports remain separately dated evidence.

Around 1600 CE lies at the end of the selected Benin saltcellar’s approximate 1525–1600 range and within the broad date range of the Kongo crucifix. Neither is securely made in this exact year. The Kongo catechism of 1624 is a later comparison.

Around 1600 CE belongs to the continuing Plantin-Moretus publishing enterprise, after Christophe Plantin’s death in 1589. The Royal Society’s first meeting in 1660 is later; it cannot be treated as an institution already operating at this snapshot.

citations.locator: Plantin dates and firm continuation to 1867

text: Around 1600 CE follows Isfahan’s capital transfer of 1597–98 and overlaps selected Ottoman and Bukhara institutional histories. New Julfa’s early-seventeenth-century forced relocation and later merchant networks come afterward; they do not describe the quarter in 1600.

Around 1600 CE falls near the end of Akbar’s reign of 1556–1605. The workshop history includes earlier work at Fatehpur Sikri and Lahore, but the selected page must retain its own catalogue range. Neither residence nor every illustrated book is dated simply by the reign.

Around 1600 CE falls within Ming rule and the museum’s Momoyama art-period frame in Japan. The selected Ming object has its own date; later Qing and Tokugawa institutions should not be imported into the snapshot as though their full later arrangements already existed.

Around 1600 CE follows the first Dutch visit to Banda in 1599 and the San Agustín wreck in 1595. The VOC’s later creation and Banda conquest of 1621 have not yet occurred. This earlier exchange setting is independently described rather than produced by extending the 1621 case backward.

In 1800, Saint-Domingue was still in the revolutionary struggle. The 1794 abolition decree preceded this moment; Haitian independence in 1804 had not yet been declared. Legal status, military control and the work of plantation communities cannot be reduced to a single date.

Around 1900, the 1896 Plessy decision remained a legal reference for enforced racial separation in the United States. Brown’s rejection of separate public schooling came in 1954. The intervening history must not be presented as though desegregation was already secured in 1900.

citations.locator: Historical introduction and opinion on Plessy

text: In 1947 the Ninth Circuit upheld the ruling won by Mexican American families challenging segregation in Orange County schools. Mendez was a federal appeals decision, not the later US Supreme Court ruling in Brown and not a ruling integrating every school in the Americas.

In June 1950, the US Supreme Court ruled that Texas must admit Heman Sweatt to the University of Texas law school. It considered educational opportunities that could not be reduced to building size or a count of books. Brown’s broader public-school ruling was still four years away.

Mexico’s 2000 presidential election brought Vicente Fox, an opposition candidate, to office. This change after decades of rule by the dominant party is a specific political event. It does not establish that access to power or public services became equal for every citizen.

citations.locator: Election of Vicente Fox and limits of change

text: Around 1800, Asante court production and gold exchange centred on institutions at Kumasi. The museum’s eighteenth–nineteenth-century weights and ornaments support this setting, without fixing their manufacture to 1800. These objects precede both the later Gold Coast colony and independent Ghana.

citations.locator: Court regulation and eighteenth–nineteenth-century object dates

text: In 1900, British control was contested in Asante. In a separate setting, National Museums Scotland records purchases from a dealer during 1897–1903 following the British looting of Benin City. The two timelines concern different societies; the documented sales do not identify every object’s route.

In the Gold Coast in 1947, the United Gold Coast Convention formed. This was organization under colonial government, before the 1948 crisis, the later CPP split and 1957 independence. It supplies a specific African political setting without backdating the independence stamp.

In early 1950 the CPP’s Positive Action campaign called for strikes and resistance in the Gold Coast; leaders were imprisoned. The 1951 election and independence in 1957 came later. Political organizing did not mean that colonial executive power had already ended.

citations.locator: Historical Setting: Positive Action and 1951 election

text: In April 2000 South Africa introduced a new coat of arms, after its first democratic election and the commencement of its final constitution. A new emblem marks a change in how the state presented itself; it cannot establish that unequal conditions had ended.

citations.locator: 2000: coat of arms on Freedom Day; constitutional milestones

text: In Britain around 1800, apprentices worked in cotton mills before the 1802 apprentice legislation. The 1833 inspection system was still decades away. The later report in the factory dossier cannot be used as an inspector’s observation from 1800.

By 1900 Britain had already extended factory regulation beyond the earlier cotton-mill measures. Parliament’s 1867 extension is one dated step. A rule’s existence does not prove compliance in every workplace, and the earlier 1836 inspection material remains evidence from its own year.

On 5 June 1947 Marshall proposed a European plan for economic reconstruction with American assistance. Truman sent a related message to Congress in December. The legislation was signed in April 1948; a 1947 snapshot should show the proposal and need for recovery, not benefits already delivered under that Act.

citations.locator: 5 June speech, December message and 3 April 1948 Act

text: On 9 May 1950 Schuman proposed placing French and German coal and steel production under common authority, open to other European participants. This is a dated proposal about resources, industry and war prevention, not evidence that every European state had already joined one organization.

citations.locator: Opening account and declaration: common High Authority

text: In 2000 the euro existed for accounting and electronic payments in participating countries including France and Germany. National cash was still in use: euro banknotes and coins were introduced on 1 January 2002. Several European countries did not share the same currency timetable.

Around 1800 Iran was under Qajar rule, after the earlier Zand setting. The court photography discussed in this reading began only after cameras arrived in the 1840s. A Qajar photograph must not be backdated simply because the dynasty already existed.

In 1900 Qajar rule continued in Iran. The Berlin exhibition identifies a court photograph from 1893 and explains how photography helped construct images of rule. It supplies nearby dated evidence, not a picture taken in 1900 or an unfiltered view of all society.

In March 1947 Truman asked the US Congress for military and economic assistance to Greece and Turkey. Turkey’s republic had been proclaimed in 1923. The message records an American policy request, not money already received by every intended recipient or unanimous Turkish support.

Türkiye’s parliamentary election table records a general election on 14 May 1950. That entry establishes a dated electoral process; it does not by itself explain every voter’s choice or the extent of participation in each community. The selected Sputnik launch of 1957 still lay ahead.

By 2000 Kazakhstan had declared independence and introduced its own currency. The national bank dates those events to 1991 and 1993 respectively, and its banknote factory to 1995. These steps connect sovereignty with production without equating a change of currency with a guaranteed rise in living standards.

Around 1800, the East India Company expanded holdings through conquest and alliance under Governor-General Wellesley. This was Company government subject to parliamentary oversight, not yet the Crown takeover of 1858 and not a single uniform control over the whole subcontinent.

By 1900 the Crown had taken over the East India Company’s Indian possessions and armed forces under the 1858 Act. The earlier Company administration should not be left unchanged on a 1900 map. Nor should the 1947 border be projected backward into this period.

In August 1947 British India was partitioned as India and Pakistan became independent. Punjab and Bengal were divided. The decisions were dated; people’s journeys, losses and efforts to find relatives extended beyond the month in which sovereignty changed.

citations.locator: Independence and Partition background; selected telegrams

text: 26 January 1950 was the general commencement date of India’s Constitution. Article 394 expressly distinguishes provisions that came into force at once. Independence in 1947 and constitutional commencement in 1950 belong to separate moments, not a shared date for all South Asian governments.

On 15 November 2000 Jharkhand became a state within India, formed from districts of Bihar. This was an internal reorganization rather than independence from India. The official formation date establishes the boundary change, not its effects on every resident.

Around 1800 in China the Qing dynasty was in power. The National Library of Australia’s account places this in the longer 1644–1911 period. The selected Japanese mill at Tomioka is a later nineteenth-century setting; its machinery cannot be used to show industry in 1800.

Around 1900 Qing rule still continued in China, while Japan’s Tomioka mill had already opened in 1872. The two dates compare an imperial framework with an institution for silk production. The opening date does not establish which employee, machine or workplace rule applied in 1900.

Japan’s Constitution took effect on 3 May 1947, following April elections and before the first Diet session under it later in May. The National Diet Library lists further legal changes needed for the new institutions. Commencement therefore has a precise date without implying instantaneous implementation.

On 25 June 1950 the UN Security Council adopted resolution 82 in response to the armed attack on the Republic of Korea, calling for a halt to hostilities and withdrawal of North Korean forces. This records an institutional response to war, not a ceasefire already carried out.

citations.locator: Action note 25 June 1950; resolution title and operative demands

text: In June 2000 the leaders of North and South Korea met in Pyongyang. Their joint declaration included commitments concerning separated families and cooperation. A summit and a written commitment are verifiable; the declaration alone does not prove reunification or that every family gained contact.

citations.locator: Opening and clauses 3–4 of the joint declaration

text: Around 1800 sealers and whalers were reaching Aotearoa waters; the ministry dates early arrivals to 1791–2 and describes links with the Australian port at Sydney. Te Tiriti’s 1840 signing was still in the future. Maritime contact is not a declaration of sovereignty.

By 1900 women in New Zealand had obtained the parliamentary vote under the 1893 Electoral Act, after petition campaigns. That change concerned voting rights; it did not resolve disagreements over Māori authority or mean that every political office became open at the same moment.

The Dutch launched a major military operation in Indonesia in July 1947, nearly two years after the independence proclamation. The 1949 federal settlement and 1950 unitary state were still in the future. A proclamation, control of territory and international recognition are different historical claims.

In 1950 Indonesia ended the federal structure created by the 1949 settlement and became a unitary state. Western Samoa remained under New Zealand administration; its independence would take effect in 1962. The two settings cannot share one decolonization date.

In 2000 East Timor was under the UN transitional administration established in 1999, following the popular consultation. Independent Timor-Leste dates to May 2002. The 2000 transition was neither the Indonesian revolution of 1945–50 nor independence already achieved.

citations.locator: UNTAET:1999–2002, February 2000 and independence in May 2002
